I live in Michigan, USA and I have no idea how one becomes a bartender. I hear they make decent money, they get a lot of exposure to a wide range of individuals, and it would help me hone in my people skills. What are some pre-requisites to becoming a bartender?

I personally do not have professional experience bartending, but I do know that becoming TIPS certified is a possible place to start.

Attend bartender school. Not required to get a bartending job, but it can help. A good bartender school will provide you with the essential skills you need, probably offer TIPS certification and help with job placement. A quick look in the Michigan area and I found this school. http://www.abcbartendingnationwide.com/detroit.php

If you are not interested in taking a bartending course, then my advice would be to apply to be a Barback at your local bars/clubs. It's a low bar entry position, where you can learn a lot of on the job training.
I would disagree on the part about bartending school. I live in Wisconsin granted, but those degrees are treated like shit. Barbacking is the way to go in terms of getting a job and experience

Considering the cost of attending some of these schools, the real value has to be balanced against it's potential contribution to your career.
Not essential, but I had a lot of fun at bartending school and got TIPS certified while I was there.

I'd say don't go to bartending school. Not that it doesn't teach you anything you need to know or good skills it's just school can't beat experience. I'm on the side of not going to culinary school either. I'd say go to any of the bars you can get into and start as a bar back. You'll do most of the cleaning and stacking glasses but you will get the experience to move up. When the place you work at as bar back needs a new bartender you'll be first in line for the job. Plus barbacks make decent tips and really don't have to deal with the patrons. Bartenders will ask you to pour beers or shots and will teach you what you want to learn. Experience is everything though.

Find the manager of a bar or a restaurant with a bar. Ask them what they are looking for. This is a guy who would potentially hire you. He knows what makes a good employee and can tell you quickly. Is there anyone here who has hired a bartender who can help?

Start out as a barback. Hope you get a bar that has an awesome bartender or two and express your interest to bartend to them and the manager. If you're lucky you'll get a chance when it's slow to learn and maybe pour a few drinks. You should start this soon to be in a spot where you can bartend by next summer. Beyond that brush up on your mixed drinks and go in with some knowledge, maybe 20 or so popular cocktails. It's something you just have to learn.
